title: One Weyl normalization for both values of gcd(q+1, 3)
summary: O'Nan's recognition of PSU(3,q) (CFSG/Permutation/UnitaryThreeRecognition, theorem onan_unitary_three) splits on d = gcd(q+1,3). The coprime case builds SMapHyp (WeylAlgSetup.lean) and proves exists_weyl_normalization with the WeylAlg* files (about 1,100 lines); the case 3 | q+1 builds DThree.SMapHyp3 (DThreeSign.lean) and proves its own exists_weyl_normalization with the DThree* files (about 2,000 lines). Bridge*/Bridge3*, AssemblyOne/AssemblyThree and MainOne repeat the same chain for each case (about 800 lines).
instructions: Read both developments first. Introduce ONE hypothesis structure for the map F (keep the common fields once, and put the case-specific facts behind d or behind a hypothesis that both cases can supply) and ONE normalization theorem that covers both cases, splitting on the case only inside the steps where the arithmetic really differs. Then let one bridge and one assembly theorem feed it, and delete the duplicated case files. Keep onan_unitary_three and every protected declaration unchanged. If a full merge is out of reach, merge the largest part you can (for example the coprime case as an instance of the general bundle) and delete what becomes unused.

title: Exclude abelian Q uniformly instead of a separate q = 5 development
summary: To prove that the root group Q is nonabelian, AbelianQMain.lean has a uniform argument for q ≠ 5 (exists_not_commute_of_ne_five, via card_eq_five_of_abelian), and q = 5 is excluded by a separate development AbelianQFive*.lean (Five, Action, Basis, Cert, Coord, Frame, Model, Setup: about 1,230 lines) combined in AbelianQUniform.lean.
instructions: Find one argument that covers q = 5 as well, or a much shorter proof of the q = 5 case from facts already proved (the pair stabiliser is cyclic, |Q| = q^3, Q acts regularly on the other points, the counting in AbelianQMain), and delete the AbelianQFive* files that become unused. Keep every protected declaration unchanged.
